newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan panel to discuss IPP promotion measures.
newsitem.headline: Japan panel to discuss IPP promotion measures.

text.p: A Japanese panel will soon start discussing ways to promote the fledgling independent power producers (IPP) scheme for electricity wholesaling, a Ministry of International Trade and Industry (MITI) official said on Friday.
Japan's electric power companies issued their first tender for the wholesale purchase of electricity in fiscal 1996/97 following industry deregulation in 1995.
Some 3.5 million kilowatts (kw) of power was awarded in tenders in the first year to cover a period from 1999 to 2002.
The Japanese government is eager to take advantage of the IPP scheme, which provides an alternative source of electricity at low cost, in an effort to lower domestic electricity rates.
The panel's agenda will include discussion of whether to include longer-term projects in the IPP programme, the trade ministry official said.
Most tenders issued by private power companies in the first year covered time periods that were at most seven years ahead.
The panel will also discuss other measures to promote competition and establish transparency in the IPP system, the official said.
This will include discussion of the possible establishment of a separate body responsible for selecting tender winners, among other matters.
Currently, each power company sets the maximum price for the tender and selects the winner.
The trade ministry official said that the panel would try to draft a mid-term report before the end of the year, with a final report due out in 1998.
Any changes to be implemented will probably require a revision in the relevant laws, he said.
